Or maybe the ceiling is actually the top edge of the magenta: the bar can't move up if the magenta is within 4 rows? So the rule "the bar can't become adjacent to the magenta" would explain it: the bar can't move to a position that would touch the magenta. When the bar was at rows 12-15, moving up would make it rows 8-11, which is adjacent to the magenta (rows 4-7). So it was blocked!
But wait, when the bar was at rows 12-15, columns 16-35 (before the RIGHT move), the magenta was at columns 36-39 — the bar's right edge is column 35, and the magenta's left edge is column 36. If the bar moved up to rows 8-11, columns 16-35, would it be adjacent to the magenta? The magenta is at rows 4-7, columns 36-39. The bar at rows 8-11, columns 16-35: the bar's top-right corner is (11, 35); the magenta's bottom-left is (7, 36). They're diagonally adjacent (corner contact). If adjacency includes corners, then yes, they'd be adjacent. Hmm, but if it's 4-adjacency (edge sharing), then the bar at rows 8-11, columns 16-35 doesn't share an edge with the magenta at rows 4-7, columns 36-39 (row 11 vs row 7 — not adjacent rows; column 35 vs column 36 — adjacent columns but the rows don't overlap... wait, for edge sharing the rows need to overlap: the bar's rows 8-11 and the magenta's rows 4-7 don't overlap, so no edge sharing). No wait, corner adjacency means |dr|<=1 and |dc|<=1. Bar cell (11,35), magenta cell (7,36): dr=4. Not adjacent. Hmm, so no.
Let me reconsider. Maybe the rule is simpler: the blue bar simply can't move above row 12. An invisible wall at row 11. Why would the level designer put a wall there? Maybe... the wall is the "ceiling" of the play area, and the real player is the magenta ball, which can move (via arrow keys?) — but the arrow keys moved the blue bar.
Hmm, wait. What if both move? What if the arrow keys move the blue bar, and the magenta ball is affected by gravity and bounces off the blue bar? The ball is at rows 4-7, the bar is at rows 12-15. If the ball has gravity, it should fall onto the bar. It's not falling. So the ball is frozen.
What if the ball only falls when the bar is directly below it (columns 36-39 within the bar's range)? The bar is currently at columns 20-39 — it includes 36-39! And the ball is still frozen. So no.
Let me try MOUSE. Maybe clicking on the magenta does something. Or maybe the game is actually: click on objects to select them, and arrow keys move the selected object? The blue bar might just be a "selected" object by default.
